text: This is Think Out Loud on OPB. I'm Dave
Miller. We end this week with a
follow-up to our conversation about the
proposals by the Portland Public School
District to close as many as 14 schools
along with major program consolidations
and changes to school boundaries. Nearly
8,000 students in kindergarten through
eighth grade would have to change
schools under one of the potential
scenarios. On Tuesday, we talked to the
chair of the school board about this.
Today, we're joined by the
superintendent, Dr. Kimberly Armstrong.
She'll present her preferred alternative
to the board sometime month. Dr.
Armstrong, thanks very much for making
time for us.
>> Great. Thank you. I appreciate being
invited to Think Out Loud.
>> Very few issues that we've talked about
on this show have generated as much
feedback as this one. We're going to get
into specifics as we go, but
I sort of tried to just look at
everything and to boil down what I saw
as the two biggest issues that have come
up. And the two things that emerge to me
are first, please slow down. And second,
and this is related. It's give us more
data, more detail, more information so
that we can have faith in what you're
doing and have clarity about what this
will look like. So, I want to take these
one by one starting with the speed. What
do you say to families or to people
running for governor or currently
governor who say, "Slow this down."?

work. They then had feedback sessions as

work since the summer. And so, when I
